seed_rules.why: Grief, death, illness, trauma or loss seeds never take comedic or play approaches.
Grief, death, illness, trauma or loss seeds never take light archetypes (memorable day, celebration, a new song, an embarrassment).
Medical seeds never take approaches that trivialise consent (the chief decides, an experiment, magic, animal help, a public debate).
Belief and spirit seeds never take a mocking approach.
Supernatural seeds stay unresolved: no archetype that settles who was right.
Purely personal seeds never take prayer, magic, animal labour or experiments (source L23825).
RARE harm (leaving, a death, a friendship ending, a lost heirloom) never follows a personal, playful, celebration, somber, medical or child seed.
The elder's death is only drawn where the owner's text can carry it (seeds tagged elder_death_ok); never in a celebration seed.
Seeds with an adult-only or romantic framing (a love letter, having a child, a child's companion, a wedding) never cast a child or a teenager, and never draw an unexpected birth.
Child seeds never draw an unexpected birth.
Somber and medical seeds never cast a child to argue over an adult's care or grief (RES-04, the child's own fear, is the exception).
Somber and medical seeds never draw blame archetypes (wasted supplies, mistaken confidence, embarrassment).

role_rules.why: A vulnerable role (child, teenager, elderly villager) never draws blame archetypes, and never 'leaves for a time' with an unknown fate (a generic departure does not make sense for them; an injury may).
Personalities that can read as an insult are never given to a child.
Personalities that can read as an age stereotype are never given to an elder.

pair_rules.why: Contradiction or repeat: a devout or skeptical skeptical observer.

contract.text: 1. Isola is a generally peaceful, curious tropical tribal society. Player villagers do not deliberately abuse, torture, exploit, bully, dehumanize, or discriminate against others. They may be mistaken, defensive, anxious, proud, cautious, or slow to understand; they can learn and repair harm. They may protect themselves proportionately from genuine threats.

2. Darker past events (war, neglect, exploitation, violence, abuse, displacement) may be implied through memory, behavior, or survivor testimony, not depicted graphically or enacted by player villagers. Never turn trauma into a spectacle, a collectible reward, or a requirement to forgive.

3. No racial slurs, ethnic caricatures, derogatory group labels, or offensive stereotypes. Use in-universe differences such as regional customs, dress, languages, occupations, ancestral villages, accents, foodways, and competing interpretations of island history. If children tease, the event clearly treats teasing as hurtful and permits adult support; never frame retaliation or 'grow a spine' as the only acceptable path.

4. Arrivals are limited to plausibly lost travelers, refugees, children, boats, or artifacts from other islands and unknown places. A strange artifact may suggest a modern origin, but do NOT confirm the modern world, reveal modern technology as an operating mechanic, or establish a modern outsider civilization on-screen. VV1–VV5 stay within established shores and island geography.

5. Distinguish a business's legitimate attempt to attract customers from deception. Advertising must be truthful; compensation and refunds can be meaningful. Markets can be small, barter-based, seasonal, and rooted in local island crafts and resources.

6. Recovery is not linear. Survivors control disclosure and consent. Support can include practical safety, privacy, routines, companionship, healing, accessible adaptations, and community aid; no instant cures or mandatory disclosure.

7. Distinct situations should lead to distinct consequences. The four response prompts below are MODULAR APPROACHES, not guaranteed success outcomes. Generate concrete paired outcomes conditional on skill, resources, timing, consent, personality, and history. Avoid boilerplate trust/skill bonuses.
8. The Guardians of Isola patch changes VV5 Heathens to Isolans, retains political/cultural differences, and makes affiliation voluntary; no forced conversion.
9. Do not mechanically introduce injuries, illness, physical changes, or NPC interactions that the actual game/patcher cannot represent; use narrative callbacks or supported stats when necessary.
10. Preserve prior authored stories. This volume extends the event engine rather than silently replacing all historical text.

heading.text: MODULAR COMPANION: MYSTERIES, JUSTICE, REGRET, MENTAL DISTRESS & BELONGING

contract.text: Player villagers do not deliberately murder, abuse, exploit, discriminate, bully, or torture. Any suspected crime remains unproven without evidence; past violence is only implied. Guards may protect proportionately. Detention is humane, reviewed, and never based on identity. No forced confession or forgiveness. Experiences resembling trauma, depression, hearing voices, unusual beliefs, or paranoia are described without diagnostic labels, sensationalism, or treating symptoms as proof of supernatural gifts. Offer consent-based support and leave spiritual questions open.

no diagnostic labels in any joining words
no supernatural confirmation (no archetype tagged resolves)

seeds.title: The Empty Sleeping Mat
seeds.text: A villager fails to return from a gathering, leaving their sleeping mat neatly folded.

approaches.text: Wait for daylight before risky searches.

seeds.title: The Broken Festival Token
seeds.text: A ceremonial token is discovered broken, and no one knows whether it was accidental.

approaches.text: Ask who handled it last without accusation.

seeds.title: The Missing Harvest Basket
seeds.text: Several food baskets vanish from storage, and rumors spread.

seeds.title: The Unclaimed Letter
seeds.text: An unsigned note alleges an old wrongdoing without evidence.

approaches.text: Preserve it as an unverified claim.
Ask if anyone needs safety now.

seeds.title: Footprints at the Burial Grove
seeds.text: Unfamiliar tracks appear by a memorial after a storm.

approaches.text: Ask families whether anything is missing.

seeds.title: The Boat Without a Passenger
seeds.text: An empty damaged boat washes ashore with supplies aboard.

approaches.text: Examine it without assuming an origin.
Prepare shelter for a possible traveler.

seeds.title: The Accusation Without Proof
seeds.text: A frightened visitor describes a past threat but cannot identify who was responsible.

approaches.text: Ask guards to monitor credible threats.

seeds.title: The Guard’s Difficult Choice
seeds.text: A stranger approaches a restricted food store and seems confused.

seeds.title: The Prisoner in an Old Story
seeds.text: A legend describes humane detention after a long-ago conflict, and villagers debate fairness.

seeds.title: The Price of a False Rumor
seeds.text: An unverified accusation damages a visitor’s standing.

seeds.title: The Unpopular Verdict
seeds.text: A council’s cautious decision disappoints villagers who wanted harsher action.

seeds.title: A Boundary After Fear
seeds.text: A villager wants protection from a perceived threat without revenge.

seeds.title: The Warrior Who Froze
seeds.text: A warrior regrets hesitating during a past emergency.

seeds.title: The Guard and the Horn
seeds.text: A warning horn reminds a guard of an old conflict.

seeds.title: The Fisher Who Would Not Sail

approaches.text: Invite a short voyage only if wanted.

seeds.title: The Healer Who Remembers
seeds.text: A healer regrets being unable to save someone years ago.

seeds.title: The Builder Who Cannot Return
seeds.text: A builder avoids a worksite associated with an old accident.

seeds.title: The Parent Watching the Shore
seeds.text: A parent checks the shore repeatedly after a past family separation.

seeds.title: Voices in the Quiet
seeds.text: A villager hears voices others cannot and sometimes feels frightened, though some interpret them spiritually.

approaches.text: Ask about their experience without ridicule.
Reduce distress and support daily life.

seeds.title: The Vision at the Shrine
seeds.text: A villager describes a vivid vision that some call a blessing and others worry about.

approaches.text: Let them choose whether to share.
Seek help if the experience becomes distressing.

seeds.title: The Sleepless Researcher

approaches.text: Ask an apprentice to check notes.

seeds.title: The Unbearable Feast
seeds.text: A villager finds crowded feasts overwhelming.

seeds.title: The Days Without Joy

approaches.text: Help with daily tasks without taking over.

seeds.title: The Frightening Thought
seeds.text: A villager is distressed by an unwanted thought and fears what it means.

approaches.text: Listen without treating thought as action.

seeds.title: The Diviner’s Burden
seeds.text: A villager’s unusual perceptions are called prophecy, creating exhausting expectations.

seeds.title: The Story Nobody Believed
seeds.text: A villager describes an experience nobody can verify.

approaches.text: Acknowledge feelings without confirming the claim.

seeds.title: The Healer and Shrine Keeper

approaches.text: Ask the villager what help they want.
Combine chosen comfort with practical care.

seeds.title: The Fear of Being Watched

approaches.text: Ask about rest and distress by consent.
